title: Things to Do After You Study

source.name: VOA Learning English — Things to Do After You Study
source.license: Nội dung của VOA (Voice of America), phạm vi công cộng
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Many students study with little thought about what comes after their study session.
But what you do after studying could have an effect on how well you learn and remember new information.
Today on Education Tips, we will explore two no-cost ways that can help you improve your learning: wakeful rest and sleep.
When many students finish studying, they often go straight to another activity. Perhaps they look at their phone or computer. They might even play a video game or watch television.
But research suggests that resting after you study may help you remember what you studied.

The basic idea is this: by reducing your activity after the study session, your brain gets a chance to rest. Resting is difficult when you have too much stimulation from electronic devices, games, lights and so on.
While this might sound unusual to you, many studies have explored the benefits of resting after learning – what is called “wakeful rest.”

A study published in the Journal PLOS One examined how well older people who were in good health could remember certain words. In two different experiments, researchers found that older adults who rested for 10 minutes after learning new words had better memory of those words. “A period of wakeful rest immediately after new learning boosts free recall of verbal material,” the researchers wrote.
The results were strong even after seven days, they added.

A 2019 study found that both young and older adults were able to better remember, or recollect, information from prose passages after doing wakeful rest. The findings appeared in Neuroscience Letters.
This study involved 45 younger people and 40 elderly adults.
“Wakeful resting led to higher overall recollection in both age groups,” the researchers noted.

If you want to give “wakeful rest” a try, here are a few simple things to do. Rest quietly for five to ten minutes. Do not look at your phone, read stories or play games. Just limit the amount of stimulation you get. It is really that easy!
In addition to wakeful rest, sleep is also important for learning.

The Division of Sleep Medicine at Harvard Medical School notes that sleep helps people to learn in two ways. A report on the school’s website explains that “a sleep-deprived person cannot focus attention optimally and therefore cannot learn efficiently.” It also says, “sleep itself has a role in the consolidation of memory, which is essential for learning new information.”

Robert Stickgold is a doctor and sleep expert at Harvard Medical School. Speaking with the U.S. National Institutes of Health, or NIH, he noted that new memories can be hard to keep. “When we first form memories, they’re in a very raw and fragile form,” he said.
Sleep is important for forming memories. Stickgold told the NIH “you get very little benefit from cutting corners.”

The National Sleep Foundation suggests that adults between the ages of 18 and 64 get between 7 and 9 hours of sleep per day. Teenagers may need slightly more, and people over the age of 65 may need a little less.
Try to get some “wakeful rest” after a study session. Then try to get a good night’s sleep.
That’s it – a simple, no-cost way to help you remember what you learn.

questions.q: What is the main point the writer makes in this text?
options: What learners do straight after a lesson can influence how much they retain
Using electronic devices is the quickest way to memorise new words
Older learners remember new information better than younger ones
Long study sessions are the best way to prepare for an exam
questions.explain: Toàn bài: tác giả nói việc làm ngay sau khi học (nghỉ ngơi tỉnh táo, ngủ) ảnh hưởng đến việc học và nhớ (“effect on how well you learn and remember”).

questions.q: According to the writer, why might resting quietly after studying be helpful?
options: Games and videos give the brain a different kind of exercise
A short break lets students decide what to study next
The brain is not overloaded, so it can hold on to what it has just learned
Switching off lights is more important than switching off devices
questions.explain: Đoạn 6: giảm hoạt động cho não nghỉ; quá nhiều kích thích từ thiết bị, trò chơi, ánh sáng làm khó việc nghỉ ngơi.

questions.q: What do the results of the study of older adults suggest about a ten-minute rest?
options: It improved recall only for people who already had a good memory
Its effect disappeared within a few hours of finishing the task
It worked better for the older group than a full night’s sleep
Its positive effect on memory was still visible a week afterwards
questions.explain: Đoạn 8–9: người lớn tuổi nghỉ 10 phút nhớ từ tốt hơn và kết quả “strong even after seven days”.

questions.q: Which student is following the advice about wakeful rest?
options: Ben, who watches a film straight after revising to help him relax
Mai, who puts her phone away and sits quietly for eight minutes after revising
Linh, who reads a short story for ten minutes after revising
Tom, who plays a quick game on his tablet after revising
questions.explain: Đoạn 13: nghỉ yên lặng 5–10 phút, không dùng điện thoại, đọc truyện hay chơi game → chỉ Mai làm đúng.

questions.q: The text says new memories are “in a very raw and fragile form”. Here, fragile suggests that they are…
options: not yet strong enough to last without support
too detailed for the brain to store easily
hard for the learner to explain to others
completely different from older memories
questions.explain: Đoạn 16: fragile = not strong; ký ức mới còn yếu nên cần giấc ngủ để củng cố.

questions.q: What does Stickgold mean by saying people “get very little benefit from cutting corners”?
options: Skipping the difficult parts of a lesson is a clever way to study
Saving time by sleeping less does not do much good for learning
Learners who revise fewer topics will remember all of them better
Going to bed early is less useful than studying late at night
questions.explain: Đoạn 16–17: ngủ rất quan trọng để hình thành ký ức; “cutting corners” = làm tắt, ngủ thiếu thì ít lợi ích.

questions.q: Teenagers are advised to sleep exactly as much as adults aged 18 to 64.
questions.explain: Đoạn 18: người từ 18–64 tuổi nên ngủ 7–9 giờ; thanh thiếu niên “may need slightly more”, nên không bằng đúng.

questions.q: The writer says wakeful rest works best in the morning.
questions.explain: Bài không nói thời điểm trong ngày nào hiệu quả nhất.
